subject: Private offer renewal — accommodating Q3 usage surge and tranche billing
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearstream.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer renewal — Q3 surge and tranche billing

Camila,

Thanks for taking this — we reviewed the renewal and have a scenario question. ClearStream is forecasting a ~30% usage surge starting mid-Q3 (expected July 15) due to a product launch. We'd like to keep a conservative committed baseline for July (roughly +20% over current), but have a mechanism to absorb the surge without repeated PO amendments.

Can Redwood propose a Private Offer that:
- Locks current pricing for an 18-month term but allows a usage-triggered tranche (pay-as-you-go) for incremental consumption above the new baseline
- Provides an invoice/schedule that separates committed capacity (prepaid or committed charges) from overage usage
- Gives a clear operational activation path so we can accept the AWS Private Offer and spin up the extra capacity quickly (target activation by 2027-07-10)

What's the timeline on paperwork (private offer + PO) and what docs do your procurement team need from us? If helpful I can loop in our procurement lead (Claire) — I'm cc'ing her on the next note.

Appreciate it,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, ClearStream AI
liam.oconnor@clearstream.ai
+1 415-555-0293

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@clearstream.ai>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — Q3 surge and tranche billing

Liam — thanks and great context. I've sketched an approach below that should meet your operational and procurement needs; attaching a draft term sheet for the Private Offer.

Proposal (high level):
- Term: 18 months, effective 2027-07-01
- Baseline committed capacity: +20% (prepaid/committed billing schedule can be quarterly or annual — we'll confirm with procurement)
- Surge tranche: up to +30% additional capacity billed as usage (monthly invoices), separate line item on invoice prefixed "Surge Usage"
- Activation: once the Private Offer is accepted (AWS Private Offer or signed DocuSign), we can prioritize allocation and a fast-path activation window (48–72 hours) for burst capacity; can pre-provision warm nodes for a small fee to guarantee <2s cold-start for key endpoints
- Fallbacks: automatic roll-to-compatible model variant when capacity constrained; Redwood can also enable throttling thresholds you choose to avoid runaway spend

Action items and timeline:
1) Review attached term sheet (RW_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet_ClearStream_20270514.pdf) — I included the tranche billing language and an example invoice schedule.
2) Procurement provides PO and billing/legal name — Claire if you want to send the PO file I can attach it to the Private Offer.
3) Our finance/legal (Rafael) will confirm tax/EIN details and the invoice cadence (we can do monthly usage + quarterly committed invoices).
4) DocuSign or AWS Private Offer acceptance — we can support either. If you prefer AWS Private Offer we can generate that once legal signs off; DocuSign is faster for most customers.

If this aligns I can circulate a final Private Offer and the DocuSign link by EOD Monday (5/17). Rafael — looped you for billing/tax confirmation. Marissa — adding in case we need marketplace ops assistance for AWS Private Offer workflow.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0114

Attachment: RW_Private_Offer_Term_Sheet_ClearStream_20270514.pdf

From: Claire Nguyen <procurement@clearstream.ai>

Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — Q3 surge and tranche billing

Camila, Liam — thanks. We're ready to proceed but have a couple procurement clarifications before we generate a PO: 

1) Invoice schedule: can you confirm which invoices will be issued monthly vs quarterly? We prefer a single consolidated invoice but can accept separate lines; please confirm the "Surge Usage" line will be invoiced monthly.
2) Tax / W-9 / EIN: please confirm Redwood's legal name and EIN for the PO and remit. We also need the primary billing contact and address.
3) Acceptance method: we prefer a signed PO + DocuSign rather than direct AWS Private Offer acceptance (easier for our internal tracking).

I've prepared a draft PO for signature — attaching ClearStream_PO_78945.pdf. Please review and let me know if the billing address needs edits. Once we confirm invoice cadence and legal details I'll sign and return the PO.

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Procurement Manager, ClearStream AI
procurement@clearstream.ai
Attachment: ClearStream_PO_78945.pdf
